description:
Follow-on to bd-xo6/gh-98. Reading encrypted PDFs works now; writing does not, and is explicitly refused rather than allowed to corrupt.

add_ink_annot and set_field_value return ErrorKind::Unsupported when doc.is_encrypted(). Without the guard they append PLAINTEXT objects to a document whose strings and streams must be ciphertext. The result still opens in kpdf - we read our own plaintext back through a decryptor that mangles it - and is unreadable in every other viewer. Silent corruption of a real form is the worst available outcome, hence failing loudly.

Consequence today: the maintainer can OPEN and READ their MOM work-pass form in kpdf but cannot fill it in there. kpdf-doctor --render already reports 'typing into X changes NO pixels' on all 17 text fields of that document, which is this bug seen from the render side.

To fix, encryption on write:
* Encrypt every string and stream we emit, with the per-object key for the object number we assign it.
* An incremental update appends objects; each new object number needs its own key. Object streams we generate would need encrypting as a unit, with contained objects left plaintext - the mirror of the read-side rule.
* AES needs a fresh random IV per stream, prepended. That means a CSPRNG - getrandom or rand - which is another dependency decision.
* /Encrypt itself, and the first /ID element, must be preserved verbatim: changing /ID invalidates every existing object's key.
* Alternative worth weighing first: SAVE DECRYPTED. Strip /Encrypt and write plaintext. Much simpler, loses the owner restrictions, and changes what the user's file is - so it is the maintainer's call, not an implementation detail.

Until then the refusal is correct behaviour, not a bug.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
RESOLVED by the maintainer's decision: SAVE AS DECRYPTED, warn the user, encryption is another application's job.

Implemented as DECRYPT-ON-OPEN rather than decrypt-on-save, which is the only coherent shape. Every writer here does an incremental update - appends objects to the existing bytes - and that only works when those bytes are the same kind as the ones being appended. Converting once at open means every existing edit/undo/save path works unchanged, with no special cases anywhere, and the write guards added earlier could be deleted outright.

PdfDocument::rewrite_decrypted() emits a plain sequential file: every in-use object written directly, a classic xref, trailer minus /Encrypt. Object streams and xref streams are dropped rather than rewritten - their contents are emitted as ordinary objects, so the containers have nothing left to hold, and only the xref we are rebuilding ever referenced them. Larger output (no objstm compression), fair trade for a file that opens everywhere.

Warning surfaced in three places: PdfReader::was_decrypted() for embedders, DECRYPTED_WARNING on the status line at open, and repeated on EVERY save ('saved <path> (DECRYPTED -- no password protection)'). Repeated deliberately - a note seen an hour ago is not consent.

VERIFIED END TO END on the maintainer's MOM work-pass form: kpdf-doctor --render findings went 17 -> 4. 'typing into X changes NO pixels' dropped from 17 fields to 3. Form filling on a formerly-encrypted document now round-trips.

REMAINING, separate issue: 3 fields (msiaNewIC, visaMonth, visaCountry) still render no pixels when filled, plus 6.6% solid black on p2 (suspected missing /SMask). Neither is encryption-related - they reproduce the same way on unencrypted documents - so filed apart rather than folded in here.

title: kopitiam-pdf: cannot WRITE to an encrypted PDF (annotations/forms refused)
